newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares rise, market ignores 96 results.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares rise, market ignores 96 results.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose by 0.1 percent on Saturday in quiet trade, brokers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.15 points to 153.36 points in turnover worth 621,000 dinars ($877,000). Two block trades in a tourism company accounted for nearly half of Saturday's trade.
The market, becalmed during the Moslem holy month of Ramadan, largely ignored strong 1996 results announced in recent days by blue-chip Arab Bank, Jordan Phosphate Mines and Jordan Cement Factories.
Expectations of good 1996 performances had already been factored into their share prices, brokers said.

"Arab Bank held up last year while the rest of the market slipped about five percent," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investors. Arab Bank was barely traded on Saturday after announcing a 18 percent rise in 1996 profits.
Jordan Phosphates was also barely traded, but Jordan Cement Factories rose 0.02 dinars to 3.37 dinars in trade worth 56,000 dinars, still below its normal trading levels.
"It's Ramadan. Only four contracts were exchanged in the first hour of trade," said Amad.

Jordan Industrial Resources also rose 0.02 dinars to 1.35 dinars in trade worth 61,000 dinars and rising shares outnumbered fallers by 18 to eight. Shares in another 11 companies were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.13 percent to 82.35 points.
